newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-INDIA ON TOP BEFORE STORM HALTS TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA ON TOP BEFORE STORM HALTS TEST.

text.p: A violent thunderstorm interrupted India's victory bid when they had South Africa reeling at 76 for five on the last morning of the third and final test at the Wanderers on Monday.
Set 356 to win, South Africa were four for one overnight and in even deeper trouble just four balls into the fifth and last morning.
Gary Kirsten edged a short delivery from Venkatesh Prasad straight to Vikram Rathore without addition to the score.

The third-wicket pair of Adam Bacher and Daryll Cullinan seemed to have seen off the new ball threat, but at 49 in the 16th over Bacher could not get his gloves out of the way against Prasad and deflected the ball onto his stumps after making 23.
South Africa plunged into deeper trouble when Cullinan ran out his captain, Hansie Cronje, five overs later.

Cullinan played a ball into the on side and called for a run, but bowler Anil Kumble had no trouble intercepting the ball and his throw to the wicketkeeper beat Cronje, who made only a token effort to reach the crease.
In leg-spinner Kumble's next over all-rounder Brian McMillan was easily caught off bat and pad by substitute fielder Pankaj Dharmani at short leg when he had made two.
But two balls later, rain forced the players off half an hour before the scheduled lunch interval, with Cullinan 30 not out and Shaun Pollock yet to score.
South Africa have a 2-0 winning lead in the series.
